- It reveals a striking impossibility result (max(x,y) cannot be precisely analyzed under any single-neuron relaxation) — this is the kind of fundamental insight that separates good from great papers.
- No fatal or major weaknesses; the criticisms are about minor phrasing or nice-to-have extras.
- Compared to the accepted anchors: it's as rigorous as the DC decomposition paper but with cleaner results and fewer limiting assumptions; it has a broader scope than the transformer-CoT paper's k-parity focus; it matches the clarity of the safety alignment paper but has a slightly narrower immediate applied impact.
- The paper's average strength is between the lower-accepted anchors (DC decomposition ~7.3) and the higher ones (safety ~9.5, transformers ~8.7), probably right around 8-9 territory.

Given the complete taxonomy, surprising impossibility result (max(x,y) limitation is genuinely striking), no fundamental flaws, and the fact that this fills a clear gap in the literature (most expressivity is per-relaxation, not comparative), the paper deserves a score clearly in the "accept" range but not quite as high as the strongest accepted papers that also demonstrate scalable applicability.
